newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Project A sets record ag trading volume.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Project A sets record ag trading volume.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade's Project A overnight session traded record volume for agricultural contracts Monday as the weekend passed with out an early frost, grain experts said.
"Last night (ended) one of those key weather weekends," said Joel Karlin, grain analyst with Everen Securities.
"We were down overnight on the limited prospects of a frost," said Dean Witter Reynolds analyst Jerry Gidel.
The after-hours electronic trading session, which began accepting agricultural orders in February, runs from 2230 to 0430 CDT Sunday through Thursday.
There were 3,794 contracts traded Sunday night, bringing the year-to-date total to 188,364 contracts, according to preliminary CBOT data.

"Project A proved to be very useful this summer because of the tight grain stocks situation and volatility," a trader said. "It will be interesting to see what it does over the next couple of years to determine if it's an asset or detriment."
CBOT senior vice president Patrick Catania said weather was a factor but strong international interest in the night session also bolstered volume.

"When you come toward harvest time, volumes pick up and (trading is) often erratic," said Catania, who also serves as head of market and product development. "The new dimension here is that we actually have first-hand participation from Europe and Asia."
CBOT members voted on July 31 to continue trading agricultural contracts at night despite complaints the after-hours session detracted from daily volume.
